chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
What the oppressed takes from the religion of the oppressor is more than what the oppressor takes from the worldly goods of the oppressed.

key_terms.الظَّالِم: the oppressor — one who commits injustice (zulm)
key_terms.الْمَظْلُوم: the oppressed — one who is wronged or treated unjustly
key_terms.دُنْيَا: the worldly life — material possessions and earthly gains
key_terms.دِين: religion — here referring to one's spiritual standing and afterlife account

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the oppressor and the oppressed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) offers a profound ethical insight on the spiritual consequences of oppression: while the oppressor may take worldly possessions from the oppressed, the oppressed takes far more from the oppressor's religion and spiritual standing. This teaching serves as both a warning to those who commit injustice and a consolation to those who suffer it, reminding the audience that the real loss belongs to the oppressor, not the victim.

en.bilal-muhammad: What the oppressed takes from the religion of the oppressor is more than what the oppressor takes from the world of the oppressed.
